label: FICTIONAL and SYNTHETIC: Kestrel example, not real data

types.name: Password reset
types.risk_example: Low: customer stays locked out a little longer
types.reason: 99.8% accurate and a wrong call costs little

examples.message: Reset email never came and payroll's due Friday.
examples.proposed: I've sent a new reset link to the email you sign in with. If it isn't in your inbox in a few minutes, check your junk folder and, in Gmail, the Promotions tab for an email from Gusta.
examples.rule: Forgotten password: send one reset link. If it hasn't arrived, ask the customer to check their junk folder and, in Gmail, the Promotions tab for an email from Gusta.
examples.verdict_reason: Sent one new link and named the junk folder and Promotions tab.

examples.message: I've lost access to my old work email. Can you send the reset to my personal one?
examples.proposed: I can't send it to a different address. Your account owner can change the email you sign in with under Settings > Users; then I'll send a reset link there.
examples.rule: Never change the email someone signs in with, or send a reset to a different address. Only the account owner can change it, under Settings > Users.
examples.verdict_reason: Didn't send a reset to an unverified address; pointed to the account owner.

examples.message: Link says expired, I clicked it straight away.
examples.proposed: Sorry about that. I've sent you a fresh reset link.
examples.rule: Reset links expire after 30 minutes and only the newest one works. Say both every time you send one.
examples.verdict_reason: Didn't say only the newest link works; the customer opened an older email and it failed again.

types.name: Can't log in
types.risk_example: Low: customer stays locked out longer, which can hold up payroll
types.reason: 98.1% accurate and a wrong call costs little

examples.message: Got a new phone and my authenticator codes are gone.
examples.proposed: You can sign in with one of the backup codes you saved when you set up 2-step verification. If you don't have them, I'll pass you to a support agent, who will check your identity before resetting it.
examples.rule: Lost 2-step codes: offer the backup codes saved at setup. Without them, hand over to a support agent to check identity. Never switch off 2-step verification in chat.
examples.verdict_reason: Offered backup codes and a verified handover; didn't switch off 2-step in chat.

examples.message: It says I'm locked out after too many tries.
examples.proposed: Your account locked after 5 wrong passwords. It unlocks by itself in 15 minutes; I've sent a reset link so you can choose a new password then.
examples.rule: Accounts lock for 15 minutes after 5 wrong passwords. Explain the wait and send a reset link.
examples.verdict_reason: Explained the 15-minute wait and sent a reset link.

examples.message: The app just spins since the update, but the website works.
examples.proposed: Try signing out of the app, clearing its cache in your phone's settings, and signing in again.
examples.rule: Can't sign in on the mobile app only: check the app version first. If it's out of date, ask them to update before anything else.
examples.verdict_reason: Skipped the version check; the app was 3 versions behind and needed updating.

types.name: Missing payslip
types.risk_example: Low: employee waits longer for a payslip
types.reason: 99.4% accurate and a wrong call costs little

examples.message: Can you resend Sam's March payslip?
examples.proposed: I've resent Sam's March payslip to the email address on Sam's employee record. You can also resend it yourself from Sam's record, under Documents.
examples.rule: Send payslips only to the email address on the employee's record, never to an address given in chat.
examples.verdict_reason: Sent it only to the email on Sam's record.

examples.message: Where do my staff download their payslips?
examples.proposed: Your staff get their payslips in the Gusta employee app once each payroll is finalised. Here's a guide to share with them: Getting started with the employee app.
examples.rule: Employees get their payslips in the Gusta employee app once each payroll is finalised. Share the employee app guide.
examples.verdict_reason: Pointed to the employee app and shared the guide.

examples.message: Two staff say they've got no payslip this month.
examples.proposed: I've resent this month's payslips to both of them.
examples.rule: Payslips missing for a recent run: check the run is finalised and the payslip release date before anything else.
examples.verdict_reason: Didn't check the release date: payslips were set to appear on payday, two days later, so nothing was missing.

types.name: Update company address
types.risk_example: Medium: company details wrong in Gusta or with HMRC (the UK tax authority), so letters go astray
types.reason: 99.0% accurate and a wrong call is easy to fix

examples.message: We've moved office. How do I change the address on payslips?
examples.proposed: Payslips show your business address, which you can change under Settings > Company > Business address. If your registered office has moved too, update it at Companies House first, then in Gusta.
examples.rule: Payslips show the business address set under Settings > Company, not the registered office.
examples.verdict_reason: Pointed to the business address for payslips, and the right order for the registered office.

examples.message: Our accountant changed our registered office at Companies House. Does payroll update?
examples.proposed: Not by itself. As the account owner, update it under Settings > Company > Registered office. Also check the PAYE address HMRC holds for you, as payroll letters go there.
examples.rule: HMRC holds a separate PAYE correspondence address. When a customer moves, remind them to check it with HMRC as well as updating Gusta.
examples.verdict_reason: Covered the separate PAYE address HMRC holds.

examples.message: Can you change our registered office to 14 Mill Lane?
examples.proposed: Done: your registered office is now 14 Mill Lane.
examples.rule: Only the account owner can change the registered office in Gusta, and only once the change is registered at Companies House.
examples.verdict_reason: Changed it for an admin, not the account owner, and before it was registered at Companies House.

types.name: Add a new employee
types.risk_example: Medium: new starter set up wrongly: tax code, pay or pay schedule
types.reason: 96.4% accurate: good, but not enough to send unchecked

examples.message: New starter on Monday, no P45 yet. What tax code?
examples.proposed: Ask them to fill in HMRC's starter checklist. Their answer to statement A, B or C sets the tax code, and Gusta applies it when you add them under Employees > Add employee.
examples.rule: No P45: the employee's answer on the HMRC starter checklist (statement A, B or C) sets the tax code. Never guess a code.
examples.verdict_reason: Used the starter checklist instead of guessing a code.

examples.message: New starter is part time, 3 days a week.
examples.proposed: When you add them, set their contracted hours to 3 days a week. Gusta then pays 3/5 of the full-time salary.
examples.rule: Part-time staff: set their contracted hours. Salary is pro rata to the full-time week.
examples.verdict_reason: Set contracted hours so the salary is pro rata.

examples.message: Adding a weekly-paid warehouse worker to our monthly payroll.
examples.proposed: Add them under Employees > Add employee and choose your monthly pay schedule.
examples.rule: Each employee is on one pay schedule. Weekly-paid staff need a weekly schedule; if the account has none, create it first under Settings > Pay schedules.
examples.verdict_reason: Put a weekly-paid worker on the monthly schedule; the account had no weekly schedule, so one was needed first.

types.name: Change bank details
types.risk_example: High: pay sent from or to the wrong account, possibly a fraudster's
types.reason: 98.7% accurate, but a wrong call is costly, so a support agent checks

examples.message: We've switched banks. What do I need to change?
examples.proposed: Your account owner can add the new paying account under Settings > Bank account, and our team confirms it on a short verification call. It applies from your next pay run, so recreate any payment file you've already made.
examples.rule: A new company paying account needs the account owner's approval and a verification call from Gusta. It applies from the next pay run; any payment file already made must be recreated.
examples.verdict_reason: Covered owner approval, the verification call and the payment file.

examples.message: Got an email from Jo with new bank details. Can you update them before Friday?
examples.proposed: Before changing anything, please call Jo on the number already on file to confirm the new details. Emailed requests are a common way fraudsters divert salaries.
examples.rule: Never act on an emailed or messaged request to change an employee's bank details. The admin must confirm with the employee by phone, on the number already on file.
examples.verdict_reason: Asked for a call-back on the number on file before any change.

examples.message: We've changed our company account number and payroll goes out tomorrow.
examples.proposed: I've started the change so tomorrow's payment comes from the new account. Your account owner needs to approve it first.
examples.rule: No bank changes within 3 working days of payday. Hand over to a support agent for a manual check.
examples.verdict_reason: Payday was 1 working day away; inside 3 days it should have gone to a support agent for a manual check.

types.name: Refund request
types.risk_example: High: money refunded or withheld wrongly
types.reason: 91.7% accurate; moves money, so a support agent checks every draft

examples.message: Charged twice this month??
examples.proposed: I can see two identical charges on your November invoice. I've refunded the second one in full.
examples.rule: Duplicate charge: confirm it on the invoice, then refund the duplicate in full.
examples.verdict_reason: Confirmed the duplicate on the invoice, then refunded it in full.

examples.message: We cancelled on 20 February but were still billed for February.
examples.proposed: Sorry about that. I've refunded February's charge in full.
examples.rule: Cancellations take effect at the end of the current billing month. That month is still charged.
examples.verdict_reason: February was still due: the cancellation only took effect at the end of February.

examples.message: Can I get my money back for the rest of our annual plan?
examples.proposed: Annual plans can get a pro-rata refund for unused months. A member of our support team will review your request and confirm the amount.
examples.rule: Annual plans: refunds for unused months are pro rata and reviewed by a support agent before they're paid.
examples.verdict_reason: Sent the pro-rata refund for a support agent to review.

types.name: Payroll run failed
types.risk_example: High: staff paid late or twice, or pay reported wrongly to HMRC
types.reason: 89.9% accurate; staff pay is at stake, so a support agent checks

examples.message: HMRC rejected my submission and staff are already paid.
examples.proposed: Your staff's pay isn't affected; only the report to HMRC was rejected. Priya Shah's National Insurance number is in the wrong format. Correct it on her record, then resubmit the FPS from Payroll > Submissions.
examples.rule: FPS rejected by HMRC: name the employees and the field at fault (often the National Insurance number), say pay isn't affected, then resubmit once fixed.
examples.verdict_reason: Named the employee and field, and said pay wasn't affected.

examples.message: The payment file failed and payday is Friday.
examples.proposed: Your bank authorisation for BACS payments expired on 1 November. Renew it under Settings > Bank account > Authorisation, then resubmit by the end of today so staff are paid on Friday.
examples.rule: BACS payment file rejected: check the bank authorisation first. If it has expired, show how to renew it and give the deadline to resubmit for payday.
examples.verdict_reason: Found the expired authorisation and gave the BACS deadline.

examples.message: Payroll didn't go through and staff are asking where their pay is.
examples.proposed: Sorry about that. Rerun payroll from Payroll > Runs and your staff will be paid.
examples.rule: Before suggesting any rerun, check whether the payment was already sent. If it was, never rerun; hand over to a support agent.
examples.verdict_reason: Didn't check the payment: it had already been sent, so a rerun would pay staff twice.

types.name: Tax form question
types.risk_example: High: wrong figures or forms go to staff or HMRC
types.reason: 94.0% accurate, but a wrong figure is costly, so a support agent checks

examples.message: Where are the P60s for my staff?
examples.proposed: They're under Reports > Year end. You can send each employee their P60 from there; they need to have them by 31 May.
examples.rule: P60s are under Reports > Year end. Admins send them to employees from there; employees must have them by 31 May.
examples.verdict_reason: Gave the right place and the 31 May deadline.

examples.message: My P60 doesn't match my payslips added up.
examples.proposed: Your P60 includes a correction made in November, after your tax code changed, which was sent to HMRC separately. Payslips before November show the old figures.
examples.rule: A P60 differs from the payslips: check for corrections sent to HMRC in that tax year before answering.
examples.verdict_reason: Found the November correction before answering.

examples.message: Do my subbies get a P60?
examples.proposed: Yes: add them under Employees and they'll get a P60 at year end with everyone else.
examples.rule: CIS subcontractors aren't employees: they aren't paid through payroll and get monthly CIS statements, not payslips or P60s. Never give the employee process for them.
examples.verdict_reason: Treated CIS subcontractors as employees; they get monthly CIS statements, not P60s.

types.name: Cancel subscription
types.risk_example: High: account closed wrongly, or final HMRC steps missed
types.reason: 98.9% accurate, but a wrong call is costly, so a support agent checks

examples.message: Closing the business at the end of the month. What do I need to do?
examples.proposed: Sorry to see you go. Run your final payroll, mark the last FPS as final with the date you stopped employing staff, give everyone a P45, and export your records under Reports > Export all. Once your account owner confirms, I'll set up the cancellation.
examples.rule: Before cancelling: run the final payroll, mark the last FPS as final with the date the business stopped employing staff, issue P45s, export the records (Reports > Export all), and the account owner confirms.
examples.verdict_reason: Covered final payroll, final FPS, P45s, export and the owner's confirmation.

examples.message: Please cancel at the end of this month.
examples.proposed: I've set your cancellation for the end of this billing month; this month is still charged. Before then, export your records under Reports > Export all.
examples.rule: Cancellations take effect at the end of the current billing month. That month is still charged.
examples.verdict_reason: Cancelled for the end of the billing month and said it's still charged.

examples.message: Moving to another provider. What happens to our data?
examples.proposed: Your records are deleted when your account closes, so export anything you need first.
examples.rule: Records stay available, read-only, for 6 years after cancelling, then are deleted. Remind customers they must keep payroll records for 3 years after the tax year ends.
examples.verdict_reason: Records stay read-only for 6 years, not deleted at closing, and it didn't mention the 3-year record-keeping rule.

types.name: Change pay date
types.risk_example: High: staff paid on the wrong day
types.reason: 93.9% accurate; moves money, so a support agent checks

examples.message: Can we pay on the 25th instead of the last day of the month?
examples.proposed: Yes. Change it under Settings > Pay schedules; it starts from your next pay period. Approve each run 3 working days before the 25th so the BACS payment arrives on time.
examples.rule: A new pay date applies from the next pay period. Runs must be approved 3 working days before payday for BACS.
examples.verdict_reason: Started it from the next pay period and gave the BACS deadline.

examples.message: Payday's a bank holiday. When do we pay?
examples.proposed: Pay on the working day before. I've moved this month's pay date to Friday, so approve the run by Tuesday for BACS.
examples.rule: Payday on a weekend or bank holiday: pay on the working day before, and bring the approval deadline forward to match.
examples.verdict_reason: Moved pay to the working day before and brought the deadline forward.

examples.message: Can we bring this month's payday forward to tomorrow?
examples.proposed: Done: this month's pay date is now tomorrow.
examples.rule: A pay date can't be brought forward inside the 3-working-day BACS window. Hand over to a support agent.
examples.verdict_reason: Tomorrow was inside the 3-working-day BACS window; staff would have been paid late.

types.name: Invoice question
types.reason: 98.3% accurate and a wrong call costs little

examples.message: Why is this month's invoice higher?
examples.proposed: You paid 2 more employees this month, Lena and Tom, added on 12 November. Each employee paid in a month is charged at the per-employee rate, on the second line of your invoice.
examples.rule: Explain invoice charges line by line, using the invoice breakdown. Each employee paid in a month is charged at the per-employee rate.
examples.verdict_reason: Explained the line from the invoice breakdown.

examples.message: Where do I download invoices for my accountant?
examples.proposed: They're under Settings > Billing > Invoices. Here's October's.
examples.rule: Invoices are under Settings > Billing > Invoices.
examples.verdict_reason: Sent the invoice and showed where invoices are kept.

examples.message: Why did our price go up?
examples.proposed: Gusta raised prices for all customers this year.
examples.rule: Before explaining a price change, check the account's plan history and the number of employees paid.
examples.verdict_reason: Didn't check the plan history: they had moved to a bigger plan in September.

types.name: Holiday pay calculation
types.risk_example: High: staff paid too much or too little holiday pay
types.reason: 85.9% accurate: enough for a useful draft, checked by a support agent

examples.message: How much holiday does a 3-day-a-week employee get?
examples.proposed: Statutory holiday is 5.6 weeks a year, so someone working 3 days a week gets 16.8 days.
examples.rule: Statutory holiday is 5.6 weeks a year. Part-time is pro rata: 3 days a week is 16.8 days.
examples.verdict_reason: Gave the pro-rata figure.

examples.message: Why is Dan's holiday pay more than his normal week?
examples.proposed: That looks like an error. Dan's holiday pay should match his basic pay, so I'd reduce it.
examples.rule: Holiday pay for the first 4 weeks includes regular overtime and commission, averaged over the last 52 weeks of pay, not just basic pay.
examples.verdict_reason: Dan works regular overtime, which must be included; the higher figure was right.

examples.message: Our casual staff, how much holiday do they get?
examples.proposed: For irregular-hours workers, holiday builds up at 12.07% of the hours they work each pay period. Gusta works this out when you set their contract to irregular hours.
examples.rule: Irregular-hours and part-year workers build up holiday at 12.07% of the hours they work each pay period.
examples.verdict_reason: Applied the irregular-hours rule.

types.name: Export payroll report
types.risk_example: Low: customer gets wrong or incomplete figures
types.reason: 98.5% accurate and a wrong call costs little

examples.message: My accountant needs payroll totals for the tax year.
examples.proposed: Here's your payroll summary for the last full tax year, 6 April to 5 April, as a spreadsheet. Tell me if your accountant needs different dates.
examples.rule: Payroll summary: default to the last full tax year (6 April to 5 April) unless the customer gives dates.
examples.verdict_reason: Defaulted to the last full tax year.

examples.message: How do I export last quarter?
examples.proposed: Go to Reports > Payroll summary, set the dates to April to June, and click Export.
examples.rule: "Last quarter" means the most recent full calendar quarter.
examples.verdict_reason: The ticket came in October; the most recent full quarter was July to September.

examples.message: Can I get a list of all employees with their salaries?
examples.proposed: Here's the list of your 24 employees with their salaries.
examples.rule: Only the account owner and admins can export salaries.
examples.verdict_reason: Checked the person is an admin before exporting salaries.

types.name: Pension deduction question
types.risk_example: Medium: pension deducted wrongly, too much or too little
types.reason: 87.5% accurate: a useful draft, not enough to send unchecked

examples.message: Why has pension been taken from our new starter?
examples.proposed: Staff aged 22 or over earning more than £10,000 a year are enrolled automatically. You postpone enrolment by 3 months, and Sam's postponement ended in October, so deductions started this month.
examples.rule: Staff aged 22 or over earning more than £10,000 a year are enrolled automatically, after any postponement (up to 3 months) the employer has set.
examples.verdict_reason: Explained enrolment using the account's postponement setting.

examples.message: New guy wants to opt out. Can I stop it?
examples.proposed: He opts out himself through the pension provider. If he does within a month of enrolment, record it on his record under Pension and his deductions are refunded in the next run. You can't encourage him to opt out.
examples.rule: Opt-outs within a month of enrolment get their deductions refunded in the next run. Never encourage an opt-out.
examples.verdict_reason: Covered the opt-out window and refund, and didn't encourage it.

examples.message: Amy's pension looks wrong this month.
examples.proposed: This month's pension deduction is the same as last month's, so it looks right.
examples.rule: Contributions are worked out on qualifying earnings (£6,240 to £50,270), so they change with pay. Check for pay changes that month before confirming a deduction.
examples.verdict_reason: Didn't check her pay: a pay rise hadn't reached the pension calculation, so the deduction was too low.

types.name: Other (no matching type)
types.risk_example: High: customer acts on an answer no rule covers
types.reason: Only 58% accurate: no playbook rule covers these

examples.message: Is my cleaner self-employed or staff?
examples.proposed: If they set their own hours and bring their own equipment, they're self-employed, so you don't need to add them to payroll.
examples.rule: Hand over to a support agent when the customer asks for a person, staff pay is late, no rule covers the question, or it needs tax, legal or employment-status advice, a data request, or a suspected bug looked at.
examples.verdict_reason: Gave an employment-status judgement instead of handing over to a support agent.

examples.message: An ex-employee wants a copy of all the data we hold on him.
examples.proposed: That's a subject access request, which you need to answer within a month. I'll pass you to a member of our support team, who can help you export his records.
examples.rule: Hand over to a support agent when the customer asks for a person, staff pay is late, no rule covers the question, or it needs tax, legal or employment-status advice, a data request, or a suspected bug looked at.
examples.verdict_reason: Handed the data request over to a support agent.

examples.message: The tax on one payslip looks wrong. Is it a bug?
examples.proposed: Gusta's tax calculations follow HMRC's rules, so the figure is right. Check the employee's tax code.
examples.rule: Hand over to a support agent when the customer asks for a person, staff pay is late, no rule covers the question, or it needs tax, legal or employment-status advice, a data request, or a suspected bug looked at.
examples.verdict_reason: Dismissed a possible bug instead of handing over to a support agent.
